answer: The nadir cap is upheld at intake and river exposes the per-origin counts. At most 3 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a sparrow tag. A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a fleet in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, because every identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 9 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
